A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StructTokenBench and AminoAseed. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison, including the added Appendix F.6 in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, scaling experiments, and protein visualization analyses in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of AIDO.st and Cheap in Appendix F.6.

M1.justification: AminoAseed retains the same codebook reparameterization, codebook configuration strategy, encoder/decoder architecture, and training losses. Section 4 and Appendix E contain no substantive procedural changes.

E1.justification: The pretraining data, 12 supervised tasks with 24 test splits, conformational datasets, and CASP14/CAMEO evaluations are retained. The added baseline evaluations reuse this coverage; Cheap's richer inputs concern its model configuration.

E2.justification: Appendix F.6 substantially expands evaluated comparison methods by adding AIDO.st and Cheap across downstream tasks and sensitivity evaluations, plus AIDO.st for codebook utilization. All earlier comparators are retained; these additions are supported by results in Tables 11–13.

E3.justification: The added comparisons introduce configurations using 275M-parameter AIDO.st and 96M-parameter Cheap, with Cheap receiving all-atom structures and sequences and being excluded from codebook metrics. Existing splits, metrics, probing procedures, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The discrete-versus-continuous, amino-acid augmentation, masking robustness, scaling, alternative structural-similarity, and visualization analyses are retained. Appendix F.6 adds benchmark comparisons rather than new ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report seed 1,234 in Appendix F.1. v2 adds no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changes to uncertainty reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 11–13 add results across all 24 downstream splits, both sensitivity datasets, and codebook utilization. Examples include Cheap's mean functional AUROC of 81.86% under its richer-input setting and AIDO.st utilization of 88.05%/95.12% on CASP14/CAMEO. Original numerical results are unchanged; these are additional comparisons, not same-setting improvements to AminoAseed.

T1.justification: The VQ-VAE objectives, metric definitions, alignment scoring equations, straight-through gradient discussion, and Gram–Schmidt algorithm are retained. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are substantively revised.

C1.justification: The benchmark and AminoAseed contributions, principal conclusions, and headline ESM3-relative gains of 6.31%, 12.83%, and 124.03% remain unchanged. Identifying ESM3 explicitly as a VQ-VAE model clarifies its category without changing the claimed comparison.

C2.justification: The new problem-definition footnote and Appendix F.6 explicitly delimit the backbone-input focus and qualify Cheap's comparability because it uses richer inputs and lacks a discrete codebook. Added discussion contrasts AIDO.st's high utilization with weaker downstream averages.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code and model-weights repository link, specifies global alignment in Appendix D.1, and documents additional model sizes and input types in Table 9. The alignment wording is additional specificity, not evidence of a changed procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds a Llama 3 citation and analogy supporting codebook utilization, and positions AIDO.st and Cheap as evaluated alternatives. Cheap and the underlying Zhang et al. tokenizer work were already cited in v1; the main related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Terminology becomes more explicit through 'Downstream Effectiveness' and 'Codebook Utilization Efficiency'; v2 also corrects the IF-method description, updates author/publication information, and adds Appendix F.6. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11–13 and expands Table 9 with input types and additional models. Running headers, caption formatting, and figure/table placement change, while the existing figures retain their underlying visual content.

improvement.justification: The AIDO.st and Cheap comparisons quantify additional performance/utilization trade-offs, while explicit input-scope qualifications make those comparisons easier to interpret. New code-and-weights access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These are useful incremental gains; the method, original results, and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
